---
title: "Real-time statistics and spectra"
---

## Objective

Follow SeedLink streams live: mean, standard deviation and peak-to-peak over a sliding window,
and an FFT amplitude spectrum or a Welch PSD over a longer sliding window.

## Principle and equations

Each channel feeds a ring buffer of $\lceil \max(T_{stats}, T_{spec}) f_s\rceil$ samples. Every
refresh period, the last $T_{stats} f_s$ samples give the mean, the standard deviation and the
peak-to-peak value (counts, and physical with `--sensitivity`); the last $T_{spec} f_s$ samples
give the spectrum (see [Spectra](spectra.qmd)).

Gaps (a record starting more than half a sample after the previous end) are written as NaN in
the buffer: statistics ignore them, and the spectrum is skipped until the window is free of
gaps.

## Assumptions and validity

Defaults: $T_{stats}$ = 10 s, $T_{spec}$ = 60 s, table refreshed every second, figure every
2 s. The spectrum resolution is $1/T_{spec}$.

## Numerical implementation

`seedlink.realtime.RealtimeMonitor`: reception in a thread (ObsPy EasySeedLink client),
computation on demand (`snapshot`), display by the caller (rich live table, matplotlib figure
updated in place). `--record DIR` appends every received record to a miniSEED file.

## Limits, biases and uncertainty

Statistics over a short window fluctuate: the relative uncertainty of a standard deviation
over $M$ independent samples is about $1/\sqrt{2M}$.

## Validation

| Case | Test |
|---|---|
| Ring buffer wrap-around; statistics and PSD from a simulated stream; recording | `test_realtime_monitor_statistics_and_spectra` |

## Worked example

Not executed here (it needs a SeedLink server):

```bash
onthesignal rt --server 10.16.0.163 --network RD --station SN270 --channels "FH?" \
               --mode dsp --window 10 --spectral-window 60 --sensitivity 2.384e-6 --unit V
```

```python
from onthesignal.seedlink.realtime import RealtimeMonitor

monitor = RealtimeMonitor("10.16.0.163", [("RD", "SN270", "00", "FHZ")], mode="fft")
monitor.run(lambda snaps: print(snaps[0].std), refresh=1.0, duration=30)
```
